items.title: [Bug] `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` rejects the only token with target mass when the coin equals the largest float32 below 1 and emits token id `vocab_size - 1`
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

With top-k + top-p sampling, many decode steps end with a single-token nucleus. After `top_k_renorm_probs` → `top_p_renorm_probs` the surviving probability is often `0.99999994` (`1 - 2^-24`) instead of exactly `1.0`.

The acceptance test in the JIT verify kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/include/sgl_kernel/speculative/sampling.cuh`) is strict:

```cpp
const bool has_target_mass = target_prob_single > DType(0);
if (has_target_mass && (coin < prob_acc / threshold_acc || target_prob_single >= threshold_single)) {
```

`torch.rand` (float32) returns multiples of `2^-24` in `[0, 1 - 2^-24]`, so `coin == 0.99999994` happens with probability `2^-24` per draw. Then `coin < 0.99999994` is false and `0.99999994 >= threshold_single` (default `1.0`) is false, so the only token with target mass is rejected. The kernel copies its probability into `draft_probs`, the residual `relu(target - draft)` is identically zero, `DeviceSamplingFromProb` finds no valid index, and the fallback `sampled_id = d - 1` emits the last vocabulary id.

**Expected:** a draft token that carries all of the target mass is always accepted (or, if rejected, is the token that gets re-sampled).

**Rate in real serving:** about `2^-24 ≈ 6e-8` per decode step that has a one-token nucleus with renormalized probability `1 - 2^-24`, i.e. roughly one unrelated token per ~10^7 generated tokens. Rare, but the emitted token has nothing to do with the distribution.

**Related:** #35771 / #35798 fixed the opposite edge (a draft token with zero target probability was accepted when `coin == 0.0`) by adding `has_target_mass` and switching `<=` to `<`. That strict comparison is what makes `coin == 1 - 2^-24` reject a token whose renormalized probability is also `1 - 2^-24`. The check is present on `main` and on tag `v0.5.21`.

**Suggested fix (any of):** keep the `has_target_mass` guard but compare with `<=` on the `prob_acc` branch; accept when the residual mass after the draft is zero; or treat `target_prob_single >= 1 - eps` as certain.

### Reproduction

No model needed; one GPU. The script below builds a one-token nucleus, uses it as the draft token, and fixes the coin at `0.99999994`.

<details>
<summary>repro.py (38 lines)</summary>

```python
"""Minimal repro: tree_speculative_sampling_target_only rejects the only token with
target mass when the coin is the largest float32 below 1, then emits vocab_size - 1.

Needs a CUDA GPU; no model weights. Run inside an environment with sglang v0.5.21."""
import torch
from flashinfer.sampling import top_k_renorm_probs, top_p_renorm_probs
from sglang.kernels.ops.speculative.sampling import tree_speculative_sampling_target_only

V, N, B, TOK = 248320, 4, 8, 1174  # vocab size, draft tokens per request, batch, the nucleus token
dev = "cuda"
p = torch.full((1, V), (1 - 0.9982) / (V - 1), device=dev)
p[0, TOK] = 0.9982
q = top_p_renorm_probs(top_k_renorm_probs(p, 20), 0.95)  # single-token nucleus
print("nucleus size:", int((q > 0).sum()), " renormalized prob:", repr(q[0, TOK].item()))

target = q.view(1, 1, V).repeat(B, N, 1).contiguous()
draft = torch.zeros_like(target)
cand = torch.full((B, N), TOK, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)  # draft token == the nucleus token
ridx = (torch.arange(B, device=dev).view(-1, 1) * N + torch.arange(N, device=dev)).contiguous()
rnext = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3, -1], device=dev).repeat(B, 1).contiguous()  # chain
rsib = torch.full((B, N), -1, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)

for coin in (0.5, 0.99999994):  # torch.rand(float32) returns 0.99999994 with probability 2^-24
    coins = torch.full((B, N), coin, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
    final = torch.rand((B,), dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
    predicts = torch.zeros(B * N, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    accept_index = torch.full((B, N), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    accept_num = torch.zeros((B,), dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    tree_speculative_sampling_target_only(
        predicts=predicts, accept_index=accept_index, accept_token_num=accept_num,
        candidates=cand, retrive_index=ridx, retrive_next_token=rnext, retrive_next_sibling=rsib,
        uniform_samples=coins, uniform_samples_for_final_sampling=final,
        target_probs=target, draft_probs=draft,
        threshold_single=1.0, threshold_acc=1.0, deterministic=True,
    )
    draft.zero_()
    print(f"coin={coin!r}: accepted drafts per row {accept_num.tolist()}, first emitted token per row {predicts.view(B, N)[:, 0].tolist()}")
# Expected: token 1174 in both cases. Observed with coin=0.99999994: 0 accepted, token 248319 (= V - 1).
```

</details>

Output inside the official `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21` image:

```
nucleus size: 1  renormalized prob: 0.9999999403953552
coin=0.5: accepted drafts per row [3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3], first emitted token per row [1174, 1174, 1174, 1174, 1174, 1174, 1174, 1174]
coin=0.99999994: accepted drafts per row [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0], first emitted token per row [248319, 248319, 248319, 248319, 248319, 248319, 248319, 248319]
```

In a 1,000,448-row run of the same setup: with `torch.rand` coins every row accepts and emits the nucleus token; with the coin fixed at `0.99999994` every row is rejected and emits `248319` (= `vocab_size - 1`).

### Environment

- sglang v0.5.21 (official `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21` image; the same code is on `main`), flashinfer 0.6.18, PyTorch with CUDA 13
- GPU architecture: SM121
- Speculative decoding settings matching the repro: `speculative_num_draft_tokens=4`, `speculative_eagle_topk=1`, default accept thresholds (`1.0` / `1.0`), vocabulary size 248320

items.title: [Bug] EAGLE/MTP same-checkpoint draft keeps redundant embed_tokens/lm_head copies resident during KV pool sizing → under-sized pool, startup OOM
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

With EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding and the draft taken from the **same checkpoint** as the target (the standard MTP setup, e.g. `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`), the draft worker loads full BF16 copies of `embed_tokens` and `lm_head`. Those copies are redundant: the MTP draft is supposed to share the target's embed/head, and the sharing code frees them (`EagleWorkerV2.init_lm_head()` → `set_embed_and_head()`/`set_lm_head_from_target()`, `python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py:310-353`, `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py:170-187`).

But the free only happens in `draft.alloc_memory_pool()`, which the scheduler (`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`, `init_memory_pools`) runs **after** the target pool is sized and **after** the draft pool is allocated:

```
init_target_memory_pool()      # target KV pool sized + allocated
draft_worker.alloc_memory_pool()
    -> TpModelWorker.alloc_memory_pool   # draft KV pool allocated  <-- OOM here
    -> init_token_map() / init_lm_head() # redundant copies freed    <-- too late
```

So both pools are sized while ~2.4 GiB/rank of about-to-be-freed weight traffic is still resident. The copies exist because for serialized NVFP4 ModelOpt checkpoints the draft is built unquantized (`_mtp_quant_config`, qwen3_5_mtp.py:65-69), and `load_weights` loads the checkpoint embedding into the draft's own tensor (qwen3_5_mtp.py:344-356): 2 x (248320/2 x 5120 x 2 B) = ~2.37 GiB per rank on this model. The draft worker also does not re-profile: `configure()` reuses the target's `memory_pool_config` (`kv_cache_configurator.py:366-370`), so the draft pool is built at the same token count into an already-exhausted GPU.

Measured impact, same machine and flags with vs. without a patch that runs the release before sizing:

| | without patch | with patch |
|---|---|---|
| free mem after draft load | 2.30 GB | 2.30 GB |
| target KV pool sized to | **106501** tokens | **139000** tokens (the requested `--max-total-tokens`) |
| free mem after pool alloc | 0.07 GB | 1.93 GB |
| outcome | `torch.OutOfMemoryError` at startup | healthy |

Pre-patch crash:

```
File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 226, in alloc_memory_pool
    self.draft_worker.alloc_memory_pool(...)
File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py", line 376, in configure
    pools = self._init_pools(...)
File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py", line 2453, in _create_buffers_normal
    torch.zeros(v_shape, dtype=self.store_dtype, device=self.device)
torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 54.00 MiB.
GPU 1 has a total capacity of 15.56 GiB of which 14.38 MiB is free.
```

### Proposed fix

Release the redundant copies **before** any pool is profiled. The sharing logic already exists and is idempotent; it just needs to run earlier. One-hunk patch to `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`:

```diff
@@ class Scheduler
      def init_target_memory_pool(self):
          ...
          self._release_draft_redundant_weights()   # NEW: before sizing
          self.tp_worker.model_runner.account_preloaded_weights(...)
          self.tp_worker.alloc_memory_pool()

+    def _release_draft_redundant_weights(self):
+        """Share the draft's embed/lm_head with the target before pool sizing."""
+        draft_worker = self.draft_worker
+        if draft_worker is None:
+            return
+        # The methods live on the inner worker (EAGLEWorkerV2 wraps it);
+        # resolve via the base-class property (None on non-last PP ranks).
+        inner = getattr(draft_worker, "draft_worker", None)
+        if inner is None or not hasattr(inner, "init_lm_head"):
+            return
+        try:
+            inner.init_token_map()
+            inner.init_lm_head()
+        except Exception:
+            logger.exception(
+                "Scheduler: early draft embed/lm_head release failed; the "
+                "release path in draft.alloc_memory_pool still runs"
+            )
+            return
+        logger.info("Scheduler: released draft embed/lm_head copies before pool profiling")
```

Why it is safe:

- **Idempotent.** The later `init_lm_head()` inside `draft.alloc_memory_pool` re-binds the same target tensors and repeats a harmless `empty_cache()`; the early call is a no-op for it.
- **Guards the inner worker.** The scheduler's `self.draft_worker` is the outer `EAGLEWorkerV2`; the methods live on the inner worker behind the `draft_worker` property (`base_spec_worker.py:191`). The `hasattr` check skips any draft without a share path (standalone EAGLE / different-checkpoint drafts, PP ranks that host no draft).
- **Fallback.** The try/except keeps the original late-release path alive if the early one fails.

Alternative: skip materializing the copies at load time (draft loader binds the target's embed tensor directly and skips allocating the draft `lm_head`, qwen3_5_mtp.py:344-356). That removes the waste at the source but is invasive (loader paths, PP stages, tie-words), whereas the scheduler-side fix is one guarded call site that works for every model family implementing `set_embed_and_head` (qwen2/3/3.5/3.8, glm, deepseek-v2/v4, gemma4, hunyuan, ...).


### Reproduction

```bash
          /home/noname/venv-sglang/bin/sglang serve \
              --trust-remote-code \
              --model-path /home/noname/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--nvidia--Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4/snapshots/482ca0f3832238542f8f5295dde86b5f22711d80 \
              --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
              --attention-backend flashinfer \
              --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
              --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
              --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
              --mamba-full-memory-ratio 4.59 \
              --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy \
              --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
              --disable-custom-all-reduce \
              --served-model-name qwen38-nvfp4 \
              --mem-fraction-static 1.0 \
              --max-total-tokens 139000 \
              --tp 2 \
              --max-running-requests 1 \
              --max-mamba-cache-size 4 \
              --enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint \
              --mamba-track-interval 32768 \
              --enable-cache-report \
              --host 0.0.0.0 \
              --port 30000 \
              --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
              --speculative-draft-model-path /home/noname/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--nvidia--Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4/snapshots/482ca0f3832238542f8f5295dde86b5f22711d80 \
              --cuda-graph-backend-prefill=disabled \
              --mm-process-config '{"image": {"min_pixels": 1048576, "max_pixels": 4194304}}' \
              --limit-mm-data-per-request '{"image": 1}' \
              --image-processor-backend pil
```

The server fails to start with the `OutOfMemoryError` above. The redundant copies are visible in the log as the draft load line `Load weight end. ... type=Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP, ... mem usage=2.81 GB` (vs `9.89 GB` for the target), followed by the pool sizing `#tokens: 106501` and then the OOM in the draft pool's `torch.zeros`. The copies are only freed later inside `draft_worker.alloc_memory_pool`, which is too late for both pool allocations.

### Environment

- sglang `0.5.22.dev306+g35f3c96ff` (2026-10-04); same code path present in `0.5.21`
- `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4` (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`, vocab_size 248320, hidden_size 5120, `tie_word_embeddings: false`, embedded MTP head)
- Python 3.12.3, torch 2.14.1+cu130, CUDA 13.0 (sglang installed editable from source)
- Flags as in the reproduction block; `kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3`, `max_running_requests=1`, `chunked_prefill_size=4096`
- With the patch applied, the same command reaches the requested 139000 tokens with 1.93 GB free at pool end, and logs `Scheduler: released draft embed/lm_head copies before pool profiling` on both ranks

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4.1 fails at attention backend init on SM12x (GB10): the candidate indexer requires DeepGEMM paged sparse MQA logits, which are SM100-only
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

I run DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with TP4 across four DGX Spark (GB10, SM121) nodes. On v0.5.21, and on main (00bcc25f6c, nightly image `nightly-dev-cu13-20261003-65f75914`), the server loads the weights and then dies while building the attention backend:

```
  File ".../srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py", line 1128, in __init__
    self.prefill_candidates, self.decode_candidates = make_candidate_indexer(
  File ".../srt/layers/attention/dsv4/v41_indexer/__init__.py", line 117, in make_candidate_indexer
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: the candidate indexer needs DeepGEMM's paged sparse MQA logits (sgl-deep-gemm >= 0.2.0 with SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM on)
```

The message suggests a configuration problem, but on SM12x there is nothing to configure. sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.0 is installed and JIT DeepGEMM is on:

```
$ python3 -c "import torch; from sglang.srt.layers.deep_gemm_wrapper import configurer as c; print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(), torch.cuda.get_device_capability(), c.ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM, c.DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL, c.DEEPGEMM_PAGED_SPARSE_MQA_LOGITS)"
NVIDIA GB10 (12, 1) True False False
```

What happens in `make_candidate_indexer`:

- `is_sm100_or_newer()` is `get_device_capability()[0] >= 10`, so SM12x skips the Hopper branch that returns the dense-blocks scheme for both prefill and decode.
- It then requires `DEEPGEMM_PAGED_SPARSE_MQA_LOGITS`. `_supports_paged_sparse_mqa_logits()` returns False unless `DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL` is set, and `DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL` is `is_sm100` only. On SM12x the flag is always False, so the backend always raises.

Before the v41_indexer rewrite, the dsv4.1 branch ran this model on SM12x with mask-based candidates.

Hopper looks like the right path for SM12x too. Since #41251, the dense-blocks decode on SM90 scores the index-K pool with the Triton `fp4_index_logits_paged` kernel, publishes the candidate mask once, and selects with the JIT top-k v2. None of that is Hopper-specific. SM12x also uses the same 64-slot index-K pages as Hopper, because `dsv41_index_page_size()` returns 64 whenever the sparse API is missing. I have a fix that does this and will open a PR with test results from the four GB10s.

### Reproduction

Any DeepSeek-V4.1 launch on an SM12x GPU with candidate blocks enabled (the checkpoint default) hits it. Mine goes through a launcher for the four-node ring. The server args that matter:

```
model_path=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash  tp_size=4  nnodes=4  ep_size=1
attention_backend=dsv4  kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3  page_size=256
speculative_algorithm=DSPARK  speculative_num_draft_tokens=6
context_length=1048576  max_running_requests=16  chunked_prefill_size=4096
moe_runner_backend=flashinfer_mxfp4
```

The error is raised in `DeepseekV4Backend.__init__`, right after the KV pools are allocated, on every rank.

### Environment

```
Python: 3.12.3 (main, Aug 31 2026, 10:18:26) [GCC 13.3.0]
CUDA available: True
GPU 0: NVIDIA GB10
GPU 0 Compute Capability: 12.1
CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda
NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.0, V13.0.88
CUDA Driver Version: 595.84
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+g65f759144
sglang-kernel: 0.4.8
flashinfer_python: 0.7.0.post1
flashinfer_cubin: 0.7.0.post1
flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.7.0.post1+cu130
triton: 3.7.1
transformers: 5.17.0
xgrammar: 0.2.7
```

(Four nodes, one GB10 each, connected in a QSFP ring. The python tree is main at 00bcc25f6c on top of the nightly image above.)

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek V4 Pro loading on Lustre takes 95 minutes despite prefetch; limiting tensor-copy workers reduces it to 3.3 minutes
items.body:
## Describe the bug

Loading a DeepSeek V4 Pro FP8/NVFP4 checkpoint from Lustre on one 8-GPU B300
node takes approximately 95 minutes inside SGLang's model-loading phase,
even with `--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints` enabled. Prefetch finishes
in approximately 62–73 seconds, while the longest wait for outstanding
per-tensor loader futures is approximately 94 minutes.

In one sequential A/B experiment on the same node and container image,
changing only the tensor-copy executor in
`DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.load_weights` from the Python default of 32 workers
per rank to two workers per rank reduced the reported model-loading time
from **5717.04 s to 199.72 s**. Startup through HTTP readiness fell from
**6115.90 s to 325.52 s**. Both arms completed and served benchmark requests.

This concerns the executor used for per-tensor weight-loader calls, which
is separate from the checkpoint-prefetch and shard-reader thread counts.
The two arms retained mmap, four prefetch threads per rank, the serial
shard iterator, TP=8, and the same server arguments. DP-attention was disabled.

## Related upstream reports

- [Issue #20842](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/20842) proposed
  coordinated checkpoint prefetch for network storage. This report covers
  a remaining slowdown with that prefetch path already enabled.
- [Issue #29268](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29268) reports
  DeepSeek loading hangs on network storage with async mmap-to-CUDA copies.
  It was closed after a suggestion to enable prefetch; the issue has no
  linked closing PR. Our case adds evidence with prefetch already enabled
  and without DP-attention. Our baseline eventually completed, so we are
  reporting an extreme slowdown rather than proving a deadlock.
- [PR #37806](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37806), currently
  open, proposes automatically enabling prefetch on NFS/Lustre. Its stated
  scope leaves `should_async_load()` and executor width unchanged. Since
  prefetch was explicitly enabled in both of our arms, auto-enabling that
  flag alone would not change our configuration.
- [PR #29821](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29821) explored
  synchronous DeepSeek V4 tensor loading for an AMD/HIP slow-tail case.
  It closed without merging. That is related evidence about copy
  concurrency, but a different backend and experiment.

At inspected upstream commit
[`e8fab85a02c23e01260fb1adb030b00886f5999d`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e8fab85a02c23e01260fb1adb030b00886f5999d/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py#L5556),
the DeepSeek V4 loader still constructs `ThreadPoolExecutor()` without an
explicit worker limit. Its
[`should_async_load()` helper](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/e8fab85a02c23e01260fb1adb030b00886f5999d/python/sglang/srt/model_loader/utils.py#L295)
still selects ordinary CPU tensors for async loading. This is a source
inspection; the measurements below use the pinned version listed under
Tested revision, not a GPU reproduction on latest main.

## Measurements

One allocation, one node, default arm first and two-worker arm second:

| Measurement | Default: 32 copy workers/rank | 2 copy workers/rank |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Startup through HTTP readiness | 6115.90 s | 325.52 s |
| Native model-loading duration, maximum of 8 ranks | 5717.04 s | 199.72 s |
| Outstanding copy-futures wait, maximum of 8 ranks | 5632.56 s | 131.71 s |
| Prefetch completion duration, range across ranks | 62.04–73.11 s | 66.59–75.82 s |
| Major page faults during copy-futures wait, sum across 8 rank processes | 143,578,881 | 318 |
| MHC JIT compile duration, maximum of 8 ranks | 289.0 s | 2.1 s |
| MHC rank synchronization, maximum of 8 ranks | 3880.9 s | 41.6 s |

The model-loading timer includes nested phases; these rows must not be
added together. The futures-wait measurement starts after iterator
consumption, so it does not cover all work performed by the executor.
Per-rank phase durations and fault deltas came from begin/end instrumentation
and process resource counters, present in both arms.

During the slow arm, sampled thread wait channels included
`cl_sync_io_wait` and `folio_wait_bit_common`. Earlier-finishing ranks then
spent a long time in MHC rank synchronization. This points to the loading
and page-fault path as a useful target, rather than treating the barrier
wait alone as the cause. We did **not** capture native CUDA stacks proving
the driver-lock mechanism described in #29268.

For a limited serving smoke test, aggregate output throughput with 1000-token
input/output requests was:

| Concurrency | Default (output tokens/s) | 2 workers (output tokens/s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 110.30 | 109.32 |
| 16 | 1244.75 | 1294.89 |
| 64 | 2976.88 | 3051.67 |
| 128 | 4847.49 | 4847.73 |

These are single observations, not statistical performance or accuracy results.

## Reproduction

Use a single node with eight B300 GPUs and the checkpoint on a Lustre mount.
The measured checkpoint was `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813-NVFP4`, revision
prefix `a6ed51e`, with **66 safetensors shards totaling 941,115,855,096 bytes
(876.48 GiB)**. The checkpoint contains mixed FP8/NVFP4 weights and E8M0
scales. It was already downloaded before either arm.

Run the pinned SGLang revision below. The command below uses generic paths and ports and omits the site's
NUMA binding. Both measured arms used identical NUMA placement:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/on/lustre/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4-pro-861b \
  --tp 8 --nnodes 1 --node-rank 0 \
  --dist-init-addr 127.0.0.1:29500 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.79 \
  --context-length 2048 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 2048 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --enable-metrics \
  --weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000
```

For the second arm, stop all server processes and apply this one-line change
inside `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM.load_weights` in
`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`, preserving the rest of the image,
checkpoint, and arguments:

```diff
-        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
+        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as executor:
```

Do not substitute the shard iterator's `num_threads` setting: it controls
a different pool. Neither measured arm used `--weight-loader-disable-mmap`,
`--weight-loader-drop-cache-after-load`, or an explicit multithreaded shard
iterator override.

Record all ranks' load completion times, prefetch completion, HTTP readiness,
and major-page-fault counters. Record page residency and JIT-cache state
before each arm; a second launch is not automatically an equivalent cold
start. A worker-count sweep and reversed-order repetitions would help
determine a suitable upstream default.

## Tested revision

SGLang commit: `582389cec557c613f87a054c6968bdbf52165f20`.

The experiment used a derivative image with phase/resource instrumentation;
both arms used the same image. An unmodified public image has not been
separately verified as a reproducer. The full environment report is omitted
from this public issue; the measured setup is one node with eight B300 GPUs,
TP8, and a Lustre checkpoint mount, as described above.

## Expected behavior and suggested direction

Loading this checkpoint should finish in a few minutes on the tested
system without manually patching the model's executor. The observed A/B
suggests that a configurable, bounded tensor-copy worker count is worth
evaluating, including its interaction with mmap and prefetch. Two workers
is a demonstrated mitigation for this configuration, not a proposed
universal optimum.

This is a follow-up to #29268 covering the prefetch-enabled DeepSeek V4
path. Is there an existing upstream control for this executor, or would
a focused PR exposing it be useful?

## Limits of the current evidence

- One default-then-two-workers pair. Execution order, JIT-cache warming,
  and unobserved Lustre server/cache state remain confounders. The lower
  JIT compile time in the second arm contributes to the broad startup
  improvement; the separately measured copy-futures wait also drops sharply.
- Initial `mincore` sampling found 66 of 229,764,643 checkpoint pages
  resident before the default arm and zero before the two-worker arm.
  This does not establish a fully cold storage stack or identical cache
  behavior during loading.
- No controlled worker-count sweep, reversed B/A run, local-NVMe control,
  or full accuracy gate has been completed.
- Latest upstream was inspected in source but has not been tested on GPUs
  for this report. The measured 28.6× load-time and 18.8× startup reductions
  describe this pair only.

items.title: response_format + tools on glm47: tool calls silently dropped, model invents a JSON answer
items.body:
## What happens

On v0.5.21 (and on main as of today) with `--tool-call-parser glm47`, a request that carries both callable tools and a JSON `response_format` never calls a tool. The model answers the format immediately with invented content.

We serve GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash behind a gateway and hit this through codex, which sends its `--output-schema` as `response_format` on every request of an agent turn. Every run came back with a schema-shaped answer having done no work. A PR reviewer reported "no findings" on a diff it had never opened.

Minimal repro against the engine, temperature 0, same prompt both times ("use read_file on note.txt, then report the secret word in it"):

```
# tools only
finish_reason: tool_calls
tool_calls: [read_file({"path": "note.txt"})]

# same request + response_format: {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {..."word"...}}
finish_reason: stop
tool_calls: []
content: {"word": "note.txt"}
```

The word is invented. The file was never read. Same result with `json_object`, on both models, streaming and not.

## Why

`to_sampling_params` in `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/protocol.py` drops the tool-call constraint with a warning when the request also carries a format, then compiles the format grammar over the whole answer. That grammar forbids every tool-call token and even the thinking-close token, so the only legal output is a bare JSON object. The model complies, and makes up content to fill it.

#34881 made `required` + format a 400, which is fair. But `auto` still warn-and-drops, and glm47 is exempt from even that because its constraint is a `full_assistant_ebnf`, so on glm47 the combination silently fabricates. #5178 asked for real support back in late 2024 and was auto-closed for inactivity.

## A fix that works

The glm47 parser already generates a full-assistant EBNF covering the whole turn. The format can be merged into that grammar instead of dropping the tool side:

```
assistant_turn ::= thinking_block ( tool_call_blocks+ | final_json_answer )
```

`final_json_answer` is the response format's JSON grammar. The rule set in `glm4_moe_detector.py` already carries JSON value rules for tool arguments (`_GLM_XML_GRAMMAR_RULES`), so typing object properties reuses the same machinery. `serving_chat.py` passes the format into `get_structure_constraint` and clears `request.response_format`, so `to_sampling_params` applies the merged grammar through the existing `full_assistant_ebnf` path. `protocol.py` needs no changes.

One catch we found the hard way: the grammar alone is not enough. With just the merged grammar, the model re-calls the tool forever. Three rounds, no answer. Prose is masked, and it never finds the JSON branch. The fix also needs to state the requirement in the prompt, that the final answer must be the JSON and nothing else. The instruction alone is not enforcement. Both together, measured on both models:

```
round 0: finish_reason tool_calls, read_file
round 1: finish_reason stop, content {"word": "quokka-a6f5ca"}   # the real word, from the tool result
```

Requests with tools only, or a format only, behave exactly as before. With no format present the generated grammar is byte-identical to today's, so there is no regression path for existing traffic.

Two smaller things worth knowing if anyone picks this up. `JsonSchemaResponseFormat.schema_` is `Field(alias="schema")`, so `model_dump_json()` emits `schema_` unless you pass `by_alias=True`, and anything downstream reading `"schema"` silently gets None and falls back to a looser grammar. And the shallow schema typing matches how tool arguments are typed today, so exotic schemas degrade to any-JSON-object rather than erroring.

We're running this as a source patch on both models in production now and it has been clean. Happy to turn it into a PR if the approach sounds right, or to reshape it to fit whatever direction the maintainers prefer.

## Environment

sglang v0.5.21 (also verified on the 2026-09-25 nightly and on main), GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash, `--tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45`, TP 4 and TP 8.

items.title: [Feature] Integrate Cake kernels via FlashInfer: model-by-model tracker
items.body:
**End-to-end validation and issue reporting:** Our shape coverage and correctness have not yet been validated end to end in model serving. If you encounter (1) end-to-end accuracy degradation, (2) unsuitable API requirements, such as unnecessarily requiring contiguous inputs, or (3) faster kernel benchmarks but worse end-to-end performance because the shapes optimized by the kernel do not cover the actual model-serving workload, please open an issue and tag @yyihuang with the affected kernel, the missing or problematic shape(s), and relevant model/serving details or a reproducer. We will resolve reported issues within **6 hours**.

## Motivation

Track integration of Cake kernels already delivered through FlashInfer into SGLang, grouped by the models that requested them. The upstream inventory is [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254); model requirements below come from its subissues and the linked implementation PRs.

The proposed integration is through FlashInfer's public/prepared APIs. Each task should connect the relevant model operator, weight/cache layout, and execution mode to an eligible kernel, then measure the complete serving path. Upstream kernel benchmarks are useful starting points, not claims of SGLang end-to-end speedup.

**Snapshot: 2026-10-03 (UTC; October 2 in US Pacific); FlashInfer main [46340689a5ab](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/46340689a5ab5665ab39f6281dac4d021d7ae94b).** “Merged” below means available in upstream FlashInfer, not necessarily in a released wheel or integrated here. Open follow-ups are explicitly marked and are not included in the merged coverage. Most listed kernels target SM100/SM103; exact architecture, SM-count, dtype, layout, and shape admission remain API-specific. Let the serving adapter retain its existing backend for configurations outside those contracts.

Notation: `T/M` = token rows, `B` = requests, `Q` = query tokens per request, `S` = KV length. MoE tuples are **(hidden size, expert intermediate size, number of experts, top-k)**; an intermediate size marked “local” is after TP sharding. Enumerated benchmark shapes are evidence points, not an assertion that every combination is supported.

## Integration and acceptance

- [ ] Pin a FlashInfer revision/release containing the required merged APIs and register backend selection at the existing operator boundary.
- [ ] Check the selected release branch separately: [#5978](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5978) is merged into `release-v0.7.1` only and reverts the BF16 head-dim-256 small-M speculative-decode route because of an intermittent B200 hang. This is a separate route from the E4M3/page-64 DCP entries below; a merge on the release branch does not establish a fix on main.
- [ ] Prepare weights, plans, output buffers, and workspaces before graph capture; account for changing request lengths, routing, state indices, and graph buckets.
- [ ] Validate each listed model/checkpoint, quantization recipe, TP/EP/CP configuration, and state/cache layout. Cover prefill, decode, speculative verification, ragged batches, and prefix-cache reuse where relevant.
- [ ] Compare against the current engine backend on model quality, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, and memory. Record the actual selected route and unsupported configurations before changing defaults.

SGLang already has model/operator boundaries for these families. Existing integration work is linked below so this tracker can be completed by extending or landing those changes.

## 1. Kimi-K3 / Kimi-K3-NVFP4 / Kimi-K3 vision

Requirements: [NVFP4 end-to-end #4568](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4568), [TP12 #4542](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4542), [ragged MLA/DCP #4658](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4658), [NVFP4 MLA #4644](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4644), [W4A8 SiTU #5156](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5156).

Start from [`kimi_k3.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py) for KDA/MLA/LatentMoE and [`kimi_k3_vl.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3_vl.py) for the vision tower. Preserve the model's layer ordering, TP reductions, state-cache semantics, and ModelOpt checkpoint preparation.

| Integration task | Covered shape / contract | FlashInfer delivery / upstream status |
|---|---|---|
| KDA prefill and fused decode | D=128. Fused one-token decode includes H=8 for TP12, plus H=12/24/32/48/96; BF16/FP32 indexed recurrent states and width-4 convolution. Prefill consumes strided q/k/v views of packed `[T,3*H*128]` projection output without densification. Prefill checkpoint outputs are BF16; FP32 checkpoints and `checkpoint_state_indices` are not admitted by the Cake prefill route. Recurrent T=1 decode with explicit `cu_seqlens` is outside the explicit Cake contract; `auto` now respects that guard. | **Merged:** `recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` and `fused_kda_decode(..., backend="cake")`; [#5551](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5551), [#5846](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5846); selector/binding updates [#5901](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5901) and [#5919](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5919) preserve the public API and served shape contracts; explicit-`cu_seqlens` auto-dispatch fix [#5760](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5760); [API](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/kda.py). |
| Dense FP8 MLA and ragged/DCP MLA | Kimi latent=512, RoPE=64, E4M3 query/cache, page=64; registered H=12/96 decode and Q<=8 MTP paths. The separate var-Q DCP API accepts BF16 or FP8 query/cache, H<=128, registered pages 32/64/128, compact cumulative query lengths and rank-local KV metadata; returns BF16 output + FP32 natural-log LSE. Caller performs the cross-rank merge. | **Merged:** `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(..., backend="cake")`, [#5552](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5552), [#5627](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5627); `cake_mla_varq_dcp_decode`, [#5577](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5577). |
| FP8 dense projections | BF16 activations and ModelOpt E4M3 weights with 128x128 block scales. 22 TP1/TP8 projection families, evaluated at M={1,8,64,256,4096,16384}; hidden=7168, representative global K→N: 7168→49152 fused QKVG, 7168→1536 Q-A, 1536→18432 Q-B, 7168→576 KV-A, 512→24576 KV-B, 12288→7168 O. Prepare/repack weights once; preserve padding and valid output columns. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.gemm.kimi_k3_fp8_projection`, [API/shape guide](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/experimental/kimi_k3_fp8_projection/README.md), merged [#5642](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5642). |
| Fused router + expert-aligned route plan | FP32 logits `[M,896]`, top-16, sigmoid + selection bias, normalization of unbiased selected weights, deterministic lower-ID ties; block_m=8/16. **Current M admission is powers of two from 1 through 8192**, not arbitrary batches. | **Merged:** `kimi_k3_fused_router` / `prepare_kimi_k3_fused_router`; [#5531](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5531), [#5621](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5621), [contract](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/experimental/kimi_k3_fused_router/README.md). |
| LatentMoE front and tail, TP1/TP8 | BF16 input `[T,7168]` → router logits `[T,896]`, latent `[T,3584]`, shared SiTU `[T,6144/TP]`; tail reduces supplied routed partials, normalizes, projects to 7168 and combines shared output. T=1..128 decode, prefill validated through 16384. **148-SM devices only in this package**, TP1/8, no EP; final all-reduce remains caller-owned. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.kimi_k3_latent_moe` prepared front/tail APIs; merged [#5734](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5734), [contract](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/experimental/kimi_k3_latent_moe/README.md). |
| TP12 distributed LatentMoE tail | Routed latent `[M,3584]`, shared partial `[M,7168]`, reduce + norm + up-projection + shared reduction. Twelve GB200/GB300 NVL72 ranks in one NVLink domain; evaluated M=1..4096. Separate API/workspace from TP1/8; each rank must agree on M and workspace capacity. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.kimi_k3_tp12_tail`; [#5603](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5603), [#5668](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5668). |
| NVFP4 SiTU experts | TP8-local (3584, **384 local**, 896, 16), T=1..16384, BF16 in/out, SiTU gate beta=4 and linear limit=25. Uses TRT-LLM shuffled block-16 NVFP4 weights and caller-owned workspace; output still needs the engine's communication. | **Merged:** `cutlass_fused_moe(..., backend="cake")`, `cake_fused_moe_prepare_workspace`; [#5183](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5183), [#5710](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5710), [tutorial](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/docs/tutorials/cake_kimi_k3_situ.rst). |
| Small-token NVFP4 warp-decode | Separate full expert geometry (3584, **3072**, 896, 16), every integer T=1..32, SiTU beta=4 / linear limit=25. Do not substitute the TP8-local I=384 geometry. | **Merged:** `CakeWarpDecodeConfig` / `CakeWarpDecodeRunner`; [#5134](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5134), [#5593](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5593). |
| AttnRes fusion | BF16 hidden=7168, residual-block count 0..8; residual update, snapshot, softmax mixing, output norm. Main evaluation M=1..16384 powers of two with block counts {0,1,4,8}; additional odd-M and all-block-count correctness rows. Current package requires 148 SMs. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.kimi_k3_attn_res.prepare_kimi_k3_attn_res`; [#5853](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5853) plus schedule-selection refresh [#5916](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5916) (47 registered programs; API and precision unchanged), [contract](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/experimental/cake_kimi_k3_attn_res/README.md). |
| MoonViT-3D + PatchMergerV2 vision tower | 27 layers; normalized BF16 patches `[T,3,14,14]`, host grids (t,h,w), 1<=t<=4, positive even h/w<=512. T=sum(t*h*w), output `[sum((h/2)*(w/2)),7168]`. Prepare per grid layout and replan when grids change; the resolved plan must have a registered kernel key. | **Merged:** `flashinfer.kimi_k3_vision` prepared tower/weights; [#5746](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5746), [contract](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/experimental/kimi_k3_vision_tower/README.md). |

- [ ] Integrate and qualify the eligible KDA, MLA, projection, router, LatentMoE, SiTU, AttnRes, and vision paths separately.
- [ ] Keep the outstanding precision paths explicit: Kimi's 512+64 **NVFP4 MLA** remains a separate request (#4644). For **W4A8 MXFP4 SiTU**, the previous implementation was reverted by [#5681](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5681), and replacement [#5783](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5783) is still open at this snapshot.

## 2. Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 MoE

Requirements: [FP8 grouped GEMM #3712](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3712) and [Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4-V2 ragged decode #4832](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4832). Use the Qwen3.5 model's GDN and MoE boundaries. Existing [SGLang #40656](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40656) is an open **draft** integration PR for FlashInfer MTP verification; complete/extend that work before creating a competing implementation.

### NVFP4 small-token MoE

Merged [#5134](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5134) and [#5593](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5593) cover **every T=1..32 on SM100/SM103**, through `CakeWarpDecodeConfig` / `CakeWarpDecodeRunner`, for these checkpoint/operator geometries:

| Model | (H, I, E, top-k) |
|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B | (2048,768,128,8) |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B | (4096,1536,128,8) |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | (2048,512,256,8) |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B | (4096,1024,512,10) |

- [ ] Connect the NVFP4 expert path for matching layouts/geometries. A matching model name alone does not admit an FP8 checkpoint or a different TP-local intermediate size.

## 3. DeepSeek-V4 / DeepSeek-V4-Flash

Requirements: [sparse MLA metadata/correctness #4671](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4671), [NVFP4 FMHA decode #5403](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5403), [Flash-0731 MoE geometry #5184](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/5184).

items.title: [Bug] HarmonyParser streaming: arguments of a tool call on the analysis channel are emitted as reasoning
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


A built-in tool call on the analysis channel (`<|channel|>analysis to=browser.search ...<|call|>`) is parsed
differently when it is streamed, even when every marker arrives whole.

### Reproduction

```
from sglang.srt.parser.harmony_parser import HarmonyParser

CHUNKS = ["<|channel|>analysis to=browser.search", "<|message|>", '{"query":', ' "SGLang"}', "<|call|>"]

p = HarmonyParser()
print([(e.event_type, e.content) for e in p.parse("".join(CHUNKS))])
# [('tool_call', '{"query": "SGLang"}')]

p = HarmonyParser()
print([(e.event_type, e.content) for c in CHUNKS for e in p.parse(c)])
# [('reasoning', ''), ('reasoning', '{"query":'), ('reasoning', ' "SGLang"}'), ('tool_call', '')]
```

Through `ReasoningParser("gpt-oss")` the client gets the arguments as `reasoning_text` and
`<|channel|>analysis to=browser.search<|message|><|call|>` as `normal_text`, so the call reaches the tool-call
detector without its arguments.



### Expected behavior

The same events as for the whole text: nothing is emitted for an analysis block whose header names a recipient until
its `<|call|>` arrives, and the `tool_call` event then carries the arguments.


### Environment


### Environment

SGLang 0.5.20 (the latest release) and 0.5.18, CPU, Python 3.12, Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64

### Describe the bug


`DeepSeekV31Detector.parse_streaming_increment` matches the tool name with a greedy
`<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>(.*)<｜tool▁sep｜>`. When one delta carries the end of a call and the start of the next, the name group
spans the first call: the first call's arguments are never streamed and the second call's arguments are streamed
under the first call's index. `detect_and_parse` parses the same text correctly

### Reproduction

```
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.deepseekv31_detector import DeepSeekV31Detector

B, E, CB, CE, SEP = "<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>", "<｜tool▁calls▁end｜>", "<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>", "<｜tool▁call▁end｜>", "<｜tool▁sep｜>"
tools = [Tool(type="function", function=Function(name="get_weather", parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {}}))]
deltas = [B + CB + "get_weather" + SEP, '{"city": "Tokyo"}' + CE + CB + "get_weather" + SEP, '{"city": "Paris"}' + CE + E]
```

### Describe the bug

`DeepSeekV31Detector.parse_streaming_increment` matches the tool name with a greedy
`<｜tool▁call▁begin｜>(.*)<｜tool▁sep｜>`. When one delta carries the end of a call and the start of the next, the name group
spans the first call: the first call's arguments are never streamed and the second call's arguments are streamed
under the first call's index. `detect_and_parse` parses the same text correctly

### Reproduction

```
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.deepseekv31_detector import DeepSeekV31Detector

deltas = [B + CB + "get_weather" + SEP, '{"city": "Tokyo"}' + CE + CB + "get_weather" + SEP, '{"city": "Paris"}' + CE + E]
d, acc = DeepSeekV31Detector(), {}
for x in deltas:
    for c in d.parse_streaming_increment(x, tools).calls:
        e = acc.setdefault(c.tool_index, ["", ""]); e[0] = c.name or e[0]; e[1] += c.parameters or ""
print(acc)                                                                     # {0: ['get_weather', '{"city": "Paris"}']}
print(DeepSeekV31Detector().detect_and_parse("".join(deltas), tools).calls)   # Tokyo and Paris
```

Both calls, each with its own arguments, as `detect_and_parse` returns.

### Describe the bug

`Glm4MoeDetector.parse_arguments` tries `json.loads` on the raw `<arg_value>` text before the branch that keeps raw

```python
    print(v, Glm4MoeDetector().detect_and_parse(text, tools).calls[0].parameters)
# true {"x": "True"}   null {"x": "None"}   1.50 {"x": "1.5"}   1e3 {"x": "1000.0"}
```

items.title: [Bug] [Responses API] Replayed Codex turn is split into three assistant blocks (phase check in _merge_consecutive_assistant_messages), so the model learns to end its turn before the tool call
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

In human terms, if someone is using SGLang to serve local models and then uses Codex with a custom provider to serve that model, then there ends up being tool calls and/or further instructions which are completely dropped and/or ignored.  So to the Codex user, it appears that a message back from the model such as:

``` "Applied. Let me verify the final state — placement in the top-level block and that Codex still parses it cleanly."```

Results in just:

```Worked for 2m 10s • 5:05 PM```

But there is no tool call at all.  There should have been a verification that was called via one or more tools.

Since #38690, `/v1/responses` no longer merges the input items of one assistant turn into a single
chat message when the turn contains a `commentary` message followed by a tool call. Each item is
rendered as its own `<|im_start|>assistant … <|im_end|>` block.

Codex CLI replays every assistant step as three input items:

```json
{"type": "reasoning", "content": [{"type": "reasoning_text", "text": "..."}], "encrypted_content": "..."}
{"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "phase": "commentary", "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "Let me list the files."}]}
{"type": "function_call", "name": "exec_command", "arguments": "{\"cmd\": \"ls\"}", "call_id": "call_1"}
```

`_merge_consecutive_assistant_messages` in `serving_responses.py` now requires

```python
and merged[-1].get("phase") == msg.get("phase")
```

Only `message` items carry a `phase`. `reasoning` and `function_call` items have none, so
`None != "commentary"` and `"commentary" != None`, and nothing merges. With a Qwen (ChatML) template
the history is rendered as:

```
<|im_start|>assistant
<think>
…reasoning…
</think>

<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
<think>

</think>

Let me list the files.<|im_end|>
<|im_start|>assistant
<think>

</think>

<tool_call>
<function=exec_command>
…
</tool_call><|im_end|>
```

instead of one block (`</think>`, then the sentence, then `<tool_call>`).

**Impact.** Every past step in the prompt now shows "one narration sentence, then `<|im_end|>`". The
model copies that: it writes the preamble sentence and emits end-of-turn without a tool call. SGLang
labels the message `final_answer`, and Codex correctly ends the turn. To the user the agent says
"Applied. Let me verify the final state…" and then stops. It gets worse as the session grows, because
the misleading examples accumulate (28 of them in a 49k-token prompt in my case).

Early stopping is the usual symptom when `phase` is mishandled on replay; here the client replays
`phase` correctly and the server splits the turn.

**Measured.** I took a real Codex session where the turn ended early three times, and replayed the
exact request at each of those three points against the same server, 10 times each (non-streaming,
default sampling). The only variable is whether the assistant turn is split or merged.

| Replay point | Tool call emitted, current code | Tool call emitted, turn merged |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (earliest in the session) | 7/10 | 10/10 |
| 2 | 1/10 | 10/10 |
| 3 (latest, 28 orphaned narration blocks in the prompt) | 1/10 | 10/10 |
| **Total** | **9/30** | **30/30** |

After applying the fix below, the unmodified requests give 30/30.

The existing test `test_replay_preserves_different_assistant_phases` only covers a `commentary`
message next to a `final_answer` message. Nothing covers a `commentary` message next to a
`function_call` or `reasoning` item, which is the shape every tool-using Codex turn has.

`/v1/messages` and `/v1/chat/completions` are not affected; they receive text and tool calls in one
message.

### Reproduction

No GPU or model needed:

```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.serving_responses import OpenAIServingResponses as R

# One assistant turn, exactly as Codex CLI replays it in `input`.
items = [
    {"type": "reasoning", "summary": [],
     "content": [{"type": "reasoning_text", "text": "I should list the files."}]},
    {"type": "message", "role": "assistant", "phase": "commentary",
     "content": [{"type": "output_text", "text": "Let me list the files."}]},
    {"type": "function_call", "name": "exec_command",
     "arguments": "{\"cmd\": \"ls\"}", "call_id": "call_1"},
]
msgs = [R._normalize_response_message_for_chat(i) for i in items]
merged = R._merge_consecutive_assistant_messages(msgs)
print(len(merged), [sorted(k for k in m if k != "role") for m in merged])
```

Actual:

```
3 [['reasoning_content'], ['content', 'phase'], ['tool_calls']]
```

Expected:

```
1 [['content', 'phase', 'reasoning_content', 'tool_calls']]
```

End to end: serve any ChatML tool-calling model and point Codex CLI at it with a custom provider
(`wire_api = "responses"`, the only wire API Codex still accepts). Give it a task needing several tool
calls; turns end after a "Let me …" sentence with increasing frequency.

```
sglang serve --model-path <Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4> --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --context-length 262144 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

### Suggested fix

Treat a missing phase as compatible, and let the merged message adopt the phase once one is known.
A `commentary` message directly followed by a `final_answer` message still stays separate, so the
intent of #38690 is preserved.

```diff
@@ def _merge_consecutive_assistant_messages(
                 and merged
                 and isinstance(merged[-1], dict)
                 and merged[-1].get("role") == "assistant"
-                and merged[-1].get("phase") == msg.get("phase")
+                # ``phase`` only exists on message items; reasoning and
+                # function_call items carry none, so a missing phase must not
+                # split [reasoning, commentary message, function_call] apart.
+                and (
+                    merged[-1].get("phase") is None
+                    or msg.get("phase") is None
+                    or merged[-1].get("phase") == msg.get("phase")
+                )
             ):
                 prev = merged[-1] = dict(merged[-1])
+                if prev.get("phase") is None and msg.get("phase") is not None:
+                    prev["phase"] = msg["phase"]
```

With this change the repro prints `1 [...]`, and the existing unit tests still pass
(`test_serving_responses.py`, `test_serving_responses_stream.py`, `test_responses_custom_tools.py`,
`test_responses_protocol.py`: 120 passed, 14 subtests passed, same as before the change).
I'm happy to open a PR with this and a regression test if that's useful.

**Version note.** Found and measured on `0.0.0.dev1+g8874c51a9` (image
`lmsysorg/sglang@sha256:efec0e11a8e6ab1287c81830a214cf107f840a994e385a5c82a8077ded82782a`).
I have not run `main`, but `main` at `a0fcebb3bb` (2026-10-01) contains the identical check in
`_merge_consecutive_assistant_messages`, and the repro above depends only on that function.

Client: Codex CLI 0.159.3, custom provider with `wire_api = "responses"`, `store: false`.
